title: Wire-tailed Swallow — pair at Bandhavgarh
subtitle: Two wire-tailed swallows at Bandhavgarh tiger reserve, India — one mid-flight, the other perched on a thorn twig. Captured at ISO 2500 on the OM-1 Mark II at 500 mm (1002 mm equivalent), 1/3200s f/5.6 to freeze the flying bird. The motion-frozen feathers and the perched bird's eye give noise-reduction and sharpening tools two distinct handling problems on the same frame.
editor_note: I disagree with darwain on this one — I prefer the Topaz edit; the bird in flight is too soft with the DxO version.
exif_summary: OM-1MarkII with OM 150-400mm F4.5 TC at 500mm (1002mm equivalent), 1/3200s at f/5.6, ISO 2500

critique.text: As the original RAW file, this image serves as the baseline for comparison. It exhibits a very high level of luminance and chrominance noise throughout, most noticeably in the smooth out-of-focus background. This noise significantly degrades the overall perceived sharpness and obscures fine details on both birds. While the perched bird is in focus, the feather texture is muddied by the grain. The flying bird shows expected motion blur in the wings, but the body lacks crispness due to the noise. The other images in this set demonstrate various processing techniques that dramatically improve upon this original by cleaning up the background noise and enhancing subject detail. In terms of ranking how well the edits worked, the DxO DeepPRIME version (Image 3) is the most successful, providing incredible detail while remaining natural. This is followed closely by the well-balanced Adobe Denoise edit (Image 1), and finally the .tif edit (Image 4), which appears slightly over-sharpened compared to the others.

images.title: DxO PureRAW 6
images.caption: DxO using DxO DeepPrime wD3 with Lens Sharpness Optimization increased to 200 (Hard)

critique.text: Processed specifically with DxO DeepPRIME XD3, this image shows exceptional noise reduction and detail extraction. The background is immaculately clean, matching the other processed versions. Where this version truly excels is in the sharpness and clarity of the subjects. The fine feather details on the perched bird's white breast and the textures on the flying bird are remarkably crisp and well-defined, surpassing both the original RAW and the other edits. It achieves this high level of sharpness while maintaining a very natural organic look, successfully avoiding the artificial or 'crunchy' artifacts that can sometimes accompany aggressive AI sharpening. This represents the best balance of technical perfection and natural rendering in the set.

images.title: Topaz Photo
images.caption: Topaz Photo with noise reduction and custom subject sharpening using motion blur

critique.text: This image appears to have been processed with high-quality noise reduction, likely Adobe's AI Denoise given the .dng extension. The improvement over the original RAW is substantial. The heavy grain in the background is completely removed, resulting in a smooth, pleasing bokeh. Sharpness on the perched bird is good, retaining natural-looking feather detail without appearing overly processed. The flying bird is also significantly cleaner, allowing the focus on its body to stand out more clearly. Overall, it's a very strong edit that successfully balances noise reduction with natural detail retention.

images.title: Topaz Sharpen AI
images.caption: Topaz Sharpen AI which is a discontinued product was used on this one, with motion blur

critique.text: This image, likely processed with another AI noise reduction and sharpening tool to produce a .tif, effectively eliminates the heavy noise seen in the original RAW, yielding a perfectly clean background. However, the approach to sharpening appears slightly overly aggressive compared to the other edits. The fine details on the perched bird have taken on a somewhat artificial, 'crunchy', or almost painterly quality, losing some of the natural softness expected in feathers. The edges of the flying bird also look slightly harsh. While it is a massive improvement over the noisy RAW, the slightly over-processed look makes it less successful than the more naturally balanced DxO or Adobe edits.
